messages:
maria: heads-up — getting a support escalation from acme-inc: p95/p99 on /v1/generate jumped hard starting ~10:12 UTC; they report client timeouts and lots of retries. see dashboard: p95 ~190ms -> ~630ms, p99 ~1.05s.

alerts-bot: [ALERT] metric:cache.hit_rate(route=/v1/generate) dropped below 25% at 2026-03-15T10:11:44Z

alex: any deploys or infra changes just before that window? :thinking:

maria: there was a config rollout at 09:58 to change cache eviction policy from TTL+LRU to size-based eviction to cap memory. rolled to ~40% nodes.

samir: pulled flamegraphs and traces for slow tails. common pattern: cache lookup -> miss -> KV fetch -> CPU work recomputing prefix metadata -> longer total latencies. KV call itself is cheap (1-4ms) but recompute cost + repeated misses cause tail.

samir: trace excerpt:
```
root -> cache.lookup(key="user:pref:Acme%20Team:1234") MISS
kv.get(prefix_meta) 3ms
runtime.expand_prefix 26ms
model.generate 850ms
```

jess: could be key canonicalization issues. earlier we had a problem with percent-encoding vs spaces and inconsistent lowercasing creating many logical duplicates.

maria: sampled keys from recent misses: variations include trailing "\n", mixed case, percent-encoded spaces and literal spaces. pre-rollout hit rate ~87%, post ~13%.

kai: size-based eviction + exploded keyspace = immediate thrash. working set can't stay warm so hit-rate collapses and p95/p99 spike.

alex: mitigation plan: 1) revert eviction policy on affected pools, 2) temporarily increase cache allocation, 3) prewarm hottest prefixes for the impacted tenant, 4) ship a low-risk canonicalizer before cache lookup behind a flag.

maria: starting canary rollback to TTL+LRU on pool-usw2-b now. will monitor hit rate and latency.

support-team: update sent to acme-inc: "We see increased latency; rolling back a recent cache change and prewarming keys. ETA ~30m for visible improvement."

samir: recommend we also add short-term metric: unique_cache_key_growth_per_min and a derived ratio keys_per_tenant/requests_per_tenant to detect keyspace explosions.

jess: PR opened: normalize-prefix-keys (#3298). implements: trim, lowercase, unicode NFC, safe percent-decode for ascii. feature flag enable_prefix_key_norm default off, tests added.

kai: running prewarm job for top 12k prefixes observed in acme traces:
```
./scripts/prefill_cache --route=/v1/generate --file=/tmp/acme_hot_prefixes.txt --workers=12
INFO queued 12000 keys
INFO workers=12
INFO first-pass misses=94
DONE elapsed=48s
```

maria: canary rollback applied — hit_rate jumped 13% -> 58% within ~75s. p95 reduced to ~230ms and p99 to ~420ms. rolling to additional pools in 15% increments.

alex: keep rollout controlled. after normalization flag flips on canary, validate correctness vs prewarm set (no cache pollution).

samir: after stabilization, schedule runbook updates: require canary footprint >= 20% when changing cache policies, add regression alerts for unique key growth, and add automated prewarm hooks for big tenants on policy change.

jess: enabling flag on canary in 10m once prewarm completes; will watch unit tests and sampling logs.

maria: current snapshot: p95 ~205ms, p99 ~360ms, cache_hit_rate ~76%. marking thread monitoring. will file postmortem: root cause = eviction policy rollout + missing key normalization + insufficient canary sizing. mitigations documented.

alerts-bot: [RESOLVED] incident 2026-03-15-cache-thrash-1767894321 resolved at 2026-03-15T10:43:30Z

participants: maria, alex, samir, jess, kai, alerts-bot, support-team
